blocks.x: Applied AI & GenAI applied to Electronics & Semiconductors. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Semis and electronics fabrication run the tightest quality-latency loops in industry: yield analytics, tool matching and cleanroom reliability decided by telemetry at nanometer stakes. The fabs that win industrialize root-cause analytics and predictive tool health end to end.

items: Wafer-defect review by experts; rare classes unlearned.
Process telemetry, metrology and defect data siloed; excursion root-cause takes days of fab time.

blocks.x: The pattern composes AI Proof-of-Concept & Value Validation, Generative AI Platform Engineering, Conversational AI & Digital Humans from the Applied AI & Generative AI tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Yield analytics/excursion RCA, Defect classification, Predictive tool maintenance) on Dataq Compass and Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — Export controls among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Manufacturing & Industrial level this capability reads as: defect detection and completeness checks closing loops into andon and MES holds (escape rate down sharply on instrumented stations). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
